newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Spain bows out as Renault row grows.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Spain bows out as Renault row grows.

text.p: Spain scrapped on Friday plans to subsidise French carmaker Renault SA's modernisation of a Spanish plant in the face of angry European Union objections.

"The Spanish government has taken this decision because it doesn't make any sense for Spain that such a small amount of aid...becomes the centre of controversy," an Industry Ministry spokesman told Reuters.

European Commissioner Karel Van Miert threatened on Thursday to block state subsidies to a Renault plant in Valladolid, Spain, saying it was "absurd" for the firm to close a profitable plant in Belgium while investing with government aid in Spain.

Spain had asked the European Commission whether it could provide Renault with two billion pesetas, part of the carmakers' 12.5 billion peseta ($13.8 million), plan to modernise and expand the capacity of its plant.
But as outrage grew at Renault's decision last week to close its Vilvoorde, Belgium plant with the loss of 3,100 jobs, Spain scrapped the plan to avoid being embroiled in the row.

The carmaker's Spanish subsidiary Fasa Renault said it would forge ahead with its plans, shrugging aside the controversy which has prompted a one-hour union protest strike at various Renault plants and top level politicial intervention.
"Investments will continue as had been planned and the only thing that worries us is to return to normal as soon as possible," a Fasa Renault spokesman told Reuters.
Last year, Fasa-Renault unveiled a plan to invest some 140 billion pesetas in Spain between 1996 and 1999.
The plan envisaged, among other things, hiring another 500 workers for its Valladolid plant to expand production of the Clio model to 1,200 vehicles a day in 1998 from 865.
Labour costs in Spain are 25 percent lower than in Belgium, the company had forecast.

"All our requests for aid were examined with a fine-tooth comb in Brussels and there has never been any problem," the Fasa Renault spokesman told Reuters earlier on Friday. "Besides it isn't a very significant amount."
Fasa Renault has a work force of more than 12,600. Last year, it lost 4.12 billion pesetas after earning a profit of 1.69 billion pesetas in 1995.
The company has plants in the Spanish cities of Seville and Palencia in addition to Valladolid.
